name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Battlefield Communication Drone BCD-4
product_name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Battlefield Communication Drone BCD-4
description: A high-altitude communication relay drone that provides encrypted communications coverage over a 10 km radius when ground-based infrastructure is unavailable or compromised. The BCD-4 flies at 500 meters altitude and serves as an airborne cell tower, mesh network node, and satellite uplink, enabling full communications capability in areas where jamming, destruction, or simple absence of infrastructure has created communication blackouts. The drone operates for 8 hours and can be replaced by a fresh unit for continuous coverage.

specifications.info: data; mesh network; satellite uplink; 000 simultaneous users

story_hooks: A BCD-4 was deployed over a Tier 1 district during a communications blackout, providing the first reliable communication access the area had experienced in months — the question of who deployed it and why remains unanswered.
An enemy BCD-4 providing communications to hostile forces was shot down, and its communication logs contained the complete order of battle and operational plans of the opposing force.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact hexacopter with a distinctive cylindrical communications pod mounted centrally beneath the frame. The drone presents an aggressive, utilitarian silhouette with exposed motor housings and carbon-fiber struts. The central pod resembles a small thermos or ammunition magazine, housing antenna arrays and encryption hardware. Propellers are carbon-composite with matte black finish.
physical_description.dimensions: 38 cm diameter rotor span; 12 cm tall (body only); communication pod 8 cm diameter × 15 cm length
physical_description.weight_description: 5 kg total — easily hand-throwable with assisted electric launch; carries its own weight without fatigue for extended field deployment
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-fiber composite frame; titanium motor mounts; reinforced polymer shrouds around the central communications pod
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with anodized titanium accents; non-reflective coating to minimize aerial detection; exposed wiring uses braided polymer sleeves
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte gray-black frame with contrasting arctic-blue accents on propeller hubs and the communications pod; red LED indicator strip running around the pod's circumference
physical_description.interface_elements: Top-mounted status display (3 cm LCD screen showing altitude, signal strength, user count); 4 physical buttons (launch, mode select, emergency cut, reset); 2 external antenna mounts at 45° angles; micro-USB charging port recessed under rear shroud; encrypted data jack on pod underside
distinctive_features: Hexagonal rotor arrangement with variable-pitch propellers for stability in wind
Pulsing red LED ring around the central pod — visible from ground to confirm active relay status
Quantum-lock indicator: small holographic shimmer display on pod face showing encryption cipher rotation
Frequency-hopping antenna array with 4 directional elements splayed like a crown
Thermal dissipation fins visible on the rear of the pod — encryption processing generates heat
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logo (stylized star-burst) embossed on pod; military-grade serial number on frame strut; small regulatory stamp: 'GLMZ-APPROVED COMMS RELAY TIER 3+' on base shroud; FCC-equivalent QUANTA compliance seal (Φ symbol)
physical_description.condition_typical: In field use: hovering at 500m altitude with red LED pulsing; antenna array oriented in cardinal directions; slight drone vibration visible in propeller blur; dirt and dust accumulation on shrouds from repeated launches; scuff marks from hand-throw impact pads on undercarriage
